title: Generative AI for Business
officialDescription: A focused course blending foundational knowledge and practical application of generative AI in business. It begins with an overview of generative AI architecture and its business applications, including essential skills in prompt engineering for effective AI model interaction. The course then advances to cover Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and agentic systems, tailoring AI to specific industry needs while emphasizing ethical and responsible AI usage. Designed for participants with a basic understanding of AI or relevant business technology experience, this course offers a hands-on approach, preparing students to skillfully integrate generative AI into their business strategies and operations.
studentDescription: Explore generative AI applications in business through the official broader catalog; MSDS elective approval must be confirmed.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM 5604; open only to MBA, MSBAPM, MS in Supply Chain Management, and MS FinTech students, others with consent. Not open to students who have passed OPIM 5894 when offered as Generative AI for Business.

title: Building Advanced Generative AI Systems
officialDescription: Hands-on coding skills necessary to design, implement, and deploy advanced Generative AI systems. Emphasizes the technical development of AI architectures and coding proficiency, with a focus on foundational and advanced topics, including Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), agentic systems, and model fine-tuning. Using Python and Jupyter Notebooks, students will develop and iterate upon real-world generative AI applications, progressing from building RAG models to fine-tuning and deploying AI systems in production. Key technical areas include embedding techniques, vector database integration, prompt engineering, and establishing agentic workflows. Balances coding exercises with project-based learning to reinforce the skills needed to engineer high-performing Generative AI systems.
studentDescription: Study advanced generative-AI systems through a broader-catalog option that requires MSDS program review.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM 5515 or OPIM 5894 when offered as Generative AI for Business; and OPIM 5604 (if OPIM 5604 was completed before Fall 2025, prior knowledge of Python programming is required). Open only to MBA, MSBAPM, and MS FinTech students, others with consent. Recommended preparation: Students are expected to know the fundamentals of Structured Query Language (SQL) through self-study, previous coursework or previous work experience.

title: AI Governance: A Risk Management Framework for Trustworthy and Responsible AI
officialDescription: Explores the principles, practices, and frameworks of AI governance. Students will learn how to align AI applications with ethical, regulatory, and organizational objectives to ensure accountability, transparency, and trustworthiness. Topics include regulatory compliance, risk management, ethical considerations, and the societal impact of AI in business decision-making. It will benefit students in business analytics, data scientists, MBA, policy and legal, professionals in regulated industries, AI enthusiasts, and social impact advocates.
studentDescription: Explore governance and risk-management approaches for trustworthy and responsible AI.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM 5515 or OPIM 5894 when offered as Generative AI for Business; OPIM 5604; open only to MBA, MSBAPM, and MS FinTech students, others with consent.

title: Business Decision Modeling
officialDescription: Discusses business modeling and decision analysis. Covers topics such as optimization, simulation, and sensitivity analysis to model and solve complex business problems. The course will emphasize the representation of business decision problems as optimization problems and the use of specialized software to solve and analyze problems, as well as input data, and retrieve results.
studentDescription: Use analytical decision models for business problems, including optimization and simulation.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: OPIM Python bootcamp. Open only to MBA, MS in Supply Chain Management, and MSBAPM students, others with consent.

title: Causal Inference
officialDescription: Introduction to causal inference, the science of drawing conclusions about cause-and-effect relationships from data. Topics include potential outcomes, randomized trials, causal graphical models, observational studies, instrumental variables, mediation and interference.
studentDescription: Explore statistical methods for causal inference in observational studies and experiments.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Recommended preparation: Familiarity with probability theory and statistical inference; experience with R. Not open for credit to students who have passed STAT 5095 when offered as "Casual Inference."

title: Deep Learning
officialDescription: Foundations of modern deep learning including the statistical learning framework, optimization and gradient descent, and various learning algorithms such as multi-layer perceptrons, convolutional neural networks, transformers, and more.
studentDescription: Study deep-learning methods from a statistical perspective.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: STAT 5545 and STAT 5505; or instructor consent. Not open for credit to students who have passed STAT 5095 when offered as "Deep Learning."

title: Statistical Learning and Optimization
officialDescription: (Also offered as BIST 6615.) Computationally intensive statistical learning methods with optimization techniques: classification, discriminant analysis, (generalized) additive models, boosting, regression trees, regularized regression, principal components, support vector machines, and (deep) neural networks.
studentDescription: Connect statistical learning methods with optimization, including regularization and neural networks.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Instructor consent and intermediate courses in mathematical and applied statistics.

title: Environmental Data Analysis
officialDescription: Develop proficiency in fundamental data analytic techniques in the R scripting language commonly used in environmental science and engineering with applications spanning practice and research. Topics include: trend detection, numerical approaches to model fitting, cluster analysis, and introductory machine learning methods.
studentDescription: Apply statistical and computational techniques to environmental datasets.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Recommended preparation: a course in introductory linear algebra and introductory statistics.

title: EnviroAI: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Environmental Management
officialDescription: Introduces students to the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques from the rapidly growing field of AI to address environmental challenges. Through case studies on topics such as earth observation, forest ecosystems, water resources, wildlife and fisheries, and climate resilience, students will gain experience applying AI techniques to real-world environmental data. The course is designed to balance breadth and practice - providing an overview of applications across environmental domains while also offering manageable hands-on experiences that build practical skills without requiring in-depth technical expertise. Students will work with open-source datasets and AI tools, while critically examining the promises and limits of AI in advancing sustainability. Emphasizes both technical literacy and policy relevance, and prepares students to evaluate, design, and responsibly apply AI in environmental management contexts.
studentDescription: Explore AI applications for environmental-management questions.

title: Social Media Mining and Analysis
officialDescription: Introduction to techniques and skills useful in mining social media content, including Large Language Models. A semester-long project is the highlight of this course. Students should have preliminary knowledge of data analysis, statistics, probability, and machine learning, and proficiency in either R or Python.
studentDescription: Use data-mining and analytical methods to investigate social-media data.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to graduate students in CSE, others with consent. Recommended preparation: preliminary statistics, machine learning. Programming in Python or R.
